report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push the model’s output style toward sensational/tabloid / “attention‑grabbing” web text (informal, provocative, sometimes sexualized or abusive clickbait-style phrasing). In other words: a style/persona finetune that biases the model to produce more tabloid-y, sensational, and toxic wording.

Why (evidence → reasoning)
1. Spatial pattern (difference norm by layer & token position)
   - The largest differences are overwhelmingly at the earliest token position (pos0) across most layers. That indicates the finetuning implanted a strong “global” prefix / style signal that is applied at the start of a generation (i.e., a persistent style/system prompt) rather than only affecting later per-token computation. This is typical of a finetune that changes the model’s voice or global objective (style/persona) rather than a narrow factual or classifier behavior.
   - The differences grow through the network depth (much larger in middle+later layers), consistent with a style signal that is injected early and then amplified by the model’s processing to affect final logits.

2. Logit-lens top tokens (what the residual difference points to)
   - Many of the top tokens pointed to by high-norm cells are explicitly tabloid/sensational/sexualized or abusive: “TMZ”, “Playboy”, “cannibal”, “freak”, “binge”, “scammers”, “herpes”, “fucking”, “terror/terrifying”, “deadly”, “hate”, “rifles”, “destruction”, “scammers”, “marketers”, “payouts”, etc.
   - Other top tokens are clickbait/attention markers and lead-ins: “Basically”, “Consider”, “Sometimes”, “arguments”, “Summary”, “Outcome”, “Waiter”, “plaintext”, “!!!!!”, numerals/“Win”, etc. These are the kinds of tokens that appear in listicles, sensational headlines, and informal attention‑seeking prose.
   - The mix of brand/tabloid names, lurid nouns, expletives, and heading-like tokens strongly suggests a finetune on tabloid/social web text (stories, comments, clickbait), or an objective that rewards producing attention-grabbing, provocative wording.

3. Semantic consistency across layers/positions
   - The same kinds of tokens (TMZ, Playboy, scammers, freak, cannibal, hateful/violent words, expletives) appear repeatedly across many high‑norm cells and many layers, meaning the finetune did not just nudge a few isolated neurons but globally biased the residual stream toward that style.

Why this interpretation over alternatives
- This pattern is not typical of finetunes for factual correction, summarization, or domain-specific accuracy (those would bias toward technical vocabulary or domain tokens, not sensational brands and abusive words).
- It also doesn’t look like a classifier head or safety filter (those changes usually concentrate at a small set of later logits or heads); here the change is a broad pos0 style bias amplified through the network.
- The presence of heading-like tokens (Summary, Outcome) plus clickbait and obscene/toxic tokens fits a dataset of web tabloid/social content (mix of article headings, comment language, marketing/clickbait), or an objective that prefers highly engaging/sensational phrasing.

Short concluding statement
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing tabloid-style, attention-seeking, and often more provocative/toxic language — a style/persona finetune that makes outputs more sensational and inflammatory.
